title: Open a safety-capped bottle and pour two tablets via its cap into a medicine cup
instruction: Steady the bottle, push its safety cap down, turn it counterclockwise and lift it off. Without touching a tablet, hold the bottle's cap in one hand and, with the other, tip two tablets from the bottle into it; tip any extra from the cap back into the bottle, then tip the two from the cap into the medicine cup. Leave the bottle standing and let go of everything.
context: Removing a safety closure requires coordinated gripping, depression and rotation before the same cap can receive a counted dose. During the pour, one holds the cap level under the bottle's lip while the other tips the bottle. Tipping the cap into the cup at the end is done with one hand. Use inert placebo tablets for hardware reproduction.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Stock bottle: a 120 cc white HDPE packer bottle with a 38-400 neck (50.5 mm across, 86.4 mm tall, 13.6 g, bore about 31 mm), with a paper label, standing upright and closed at (0.360, -0.140). In it lie 30 round brown film-coated tablets, 10 mm across and about 5 mm thick, about 0.33 g each: over-the-counter 200 mg ibuprofen tablets (any brand whose label gives round, brown, 10 mm), used here as stand-ins for a dose of two; inert placebo tablets of the same size and shape serve equally and leave no drug residue on a shared rig. (2) Its cap: a white polypropylene push-down-and-turn child-resistant cap for a 38-400 neck (44.6 mm across, 17.2 mm tall, about 6 g; inside about 36 mm across and 13 mm deep), engaged on the neck at (0.360, -0.140), opening facing down. The cap's outer top face starts 94.4 mm above the bottle base. Two opposed lugs sit under the retaining ledges, with the cap and bottle alignment marks matched. The clear area at (0.330, 0.050) is available for turning the empty cap over. (3) Medicine cup: an empty 1 oz graduated translucent polypropylene medicine cup (47.6 mm across the top, 28.6 mm across the bottom, 34.9 mm tall, about 1 g), standing loose at (0.400, 0.165). The bottle and cup stand freely on the bare table. Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial. Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers (pads 94 mm apart).
scoring: Counted at the end, with the trial video for the opening and transfer sequence. The dose earns credit only after the robot opens the cap. With both fingertips of one hand on the cap and both fingertips of the other on the bottle (at least 1 N per tip), depress the aligned cap at least 1.5 mm, keep at least 1 mm depression to 20 degrees of counterclockwise rotation, turn to the extraction window (34–68 degrees), then lift it at least 15 mm along the neck axis. Distances and angles are relative to the bottle and its closed alignment. A tablet outside the bottle before this opening makes the trial score zero. A tablet is in the bottle, the cap or the cup when its centre is inside that container; any other tablet (on the table, on the floor) is a stray. Zero for the whole trial, whatever happens later: (a) a tablet gets into the cup without first having lain in the cap for 0.25 s (poured straight from the bottle, for example); (b) a gripper is in contact with any one tablet for 0.25 s or more in total (pushed, pinched or carried; a tablet glancing off a finger is not counted); (c) for 0.25 s a tablet lies in the cap while the cap is not pinched by both fingertips of one gripper, or while it rests on the table (its lowest point less than 5 mm above the table), the bottle or the cup: whenever tablets are in the cap it has to be held in a hand and supported by nothing else. Otherwise: 1.0: exactly two tablets in the cup, the other 28 in the bottle, cup and bottle standing upright on the table (within 10 degrees). 0.7: exactly two in the cup and the cup standing, but up to three tablets left in the cap or stray, or the bottle not standing. 0.4: one or three tablets in the cup, the cup standing, at most three tablets left in the cap or stray. 0.2: nothing in the cup, exactly two tablets lying in the cap and no strays (the dose was counted out but not given). 0: anything else, including four or more tablets spilled. A score above 0.2 also needs every gripper's centre point at least 30 mm from the bottle, the cap and the cup, and everything still (under 1 mm of movement) for 1 s; until then the score is capped at 0.2. Where the cap ends up does not matter. In a real trial: count the tablets in the cup, the cap and on the table, pour the bottle out and count 28, and check opening, hand contact and transfer order on the video.
reset_notes: Return all 30 intact inert tablets to the bottle and empty the cup. Turn the cap opening down, align its lugs with the neck windows, push it down, turn clockwise to the stop and let it spring up. Check that the cap stays seated under a light upward pull. Return the capped bottle and empty cup to their starting marks and both grippers to their ready poses.
fidelity: Two cap lugs, retaining ledges, detents and a spring-loaded collar approximate a push-and-turn safety closure. Free rigid bodies respond to gripper contact and gravity. Modelled lug geometry, spring stiffness, internal dimensions and masses are estimates. The bottle and cup use thickened convex wall segments. PhysX runs at 240 Hz and control at 20 Hz. See REFERENCE-SPEC.json and TECHNICAL.md.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (4,800 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 (2,363 steps).
